title: 1. Qualify the frozen negative warp with one 90-pair instrument
hypothesis: The frozen negative phase warp improves sustained spinning by redistributing contact dwell within each roll cycle without increasing stroke energy or drops.

prediction.rationale: D-062 motivates a prospective gain prediction; qualification still requires the standing paired-t lower bound above zero, not merely a positive point estimate.

protocol.command: gpu run 'bash -lc "source ~/IsaacLab/source_env.sh && python scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py --config config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml --study r089_warp_qualification_90 --log-dir logs/pen_spin/r089_warp_qualification_90"'
code_changes: The 90-pair instrument (lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin/clamp_qualification.py) generalised to take parent and candidate from its config block; registered as --study r089_warp_qualification_90 in scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py; settings in config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml. Parent: the D-058 incumbent asset (hashes checked). Candidate: the exact D-062 epsilon -0.35 warp, resolved from the archived run's phase_warp_source.py and constants.json, both hash-checked; the study aborts if either is missing or differs, never reconstructs it.

Three frozen 40-case Stage-3 manifests (seeds 4700, 4701, 4702; cases 0-9 unused, cases 10-39 the panel), placement-disjoint from every committed pen-spin manifest and from each other. Offline identity gate (epsilon 0 bit for bit on D-050's archived observations) rerun before any episode. Parent and candidate each run each panel in its own fresh process: six processes, 180 episodes, zero LLM calls.

One-off instrument of the existing strict rule: one paired t interval at the existing confidence level over the 90 prospectively declared differences; qualification requires a positive mean and a lower bound strictly above zero; adoption additionally requires candidate drops not exceeding the parent's over the 90 pairs. No interim decision, historical pooling, extension or retry.

Prediction: candidate minus parent pooled over the 90 pairs at least +0.05; refuted if the upper bound is below +0.05; a zero-inclusive interval is inconclusive and does not qualify. Reported: sustained success, paired wins/losses/ties, drops, failure split, in-play mean |spin|, drive and per-axis executed-action saturation, overall and per panel; qualification.json for the conditional R-090. Held-out split untouched.

falsified_by: A paired interval upper bound below +0.05 refutes the predicted magnitude. An interval including zero is inconclusive and does not qualify the warp; more observed drops blocks adoption.

notes: Primary, predeclared (90 pairs): warp minus parent -0.0222 [-0.1052, +0.0607] (29/90 vs 31/90; 6 wins, 8 losses, 76 ties). The interval includes zero and its upper bound is not below +0.05: inconclusive for the predicted magnitude, and the warp does not qualify (lower bound below zero); drops 6 vs 4 (+0.0222 [-0.0088, +0.0533]), so it would not be adoptable either. The incumbent stands.

Per panel: s4700 -0.033 (8 vs 9), s4701 0.000 (13 vs 13), s4702 -0.033 (8 vs 9); no panel favoured the warp. D-062's fresh gain (+0.0875 [+0.015, +0.160], 32 vs 25) did not replicate on 90 new pairs; the two measurements are compatible only at the low end of D-062's interval.

Pooled arms: warp 29/90, parent 31/90; off-centre tail failures 1 vs 6 and slow-spin 54 vs 49, in-play |spin| 3.93 vs 3.83: the negative warp still trades a few off-centre failures for slow-spin ones, as in D-062, without a net gain here.
Saturation: drive above 0.99 on 95-99% of recorded in-play steps in both arms; executed-action saturation 10.0% (warp) vs 8.8% (parent) of components.

Accounting: 180 Isaac episodes in six fresh processes, 0 LLM calls, about 4 min wall time. No deviation from the approved protocol; R-090 is cancelled by its own condition. Final-test split untouched.

verdicts.reasoning: Predicted at least +0.05 for the frozen D-062 warp over the D-058 incumbent on one prospectively declared 90-pair instrument; observed -0.022 [-0.105, +0.061] (29 vs 31; 6 wins, 8 losses, 76 ties), with drops 6 vs 4. The interval includes zero and its upper bound is not below +0.05, so the magnitude is neither established nor refuted by the predeclared rule, but the qualification question is answered: the warp does not qualify (lower bound below zero) and would not be adoptable (more drops), and no panel favoured it. D-062's fresh gain did not replicate; the honest reading is that it was at the high end of what a single 80-pair panel can show. The incumbent stands. Confidence 0.85 in the label; 0.95 that the warp is not an improvement of the size D-062 suggested.
verdicts.next_experiment: R-090 cancels by its own condition. With this, every stroke-side mechanism re-nominated after the direction's named branches (lead feedback D-061, waveform shape D-062/this) has failed to qualify on the adopted incumbent; the incumbent (zero-curl clamp, stroke x 1.408) stands at about 0.35-0.44 fresh success with few drops and slow spin as its failure mode. Unless the advisor can name a mechanism these results do not already predict, the direction's sequence is complete and the loop should stop and report.

Its upper bound exceeds +0.05, so the predicted magnitude is neither supported nor refuted, while the nonpositive lower bound fails strict qualification [logs/pen_spin/r089_warp_qualification_90/qualification.json]. Observed drops were 6 versus 4, independently blocking adoption under the no-more-drops rule, although the drop-difference interval also includes zero and does not establish increased drop risk [logs/pen_spin/r089_warp_qualification_90/summary.json]. The incumbent therefore stands [logs/pen_spin/r089_warp_qualification_90/qualification.json].
